questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Invention] What does LED stand for?
A. Light Emission Display
B. Light Emitting Diode
C. Luminous Emission Device
Answer: B. An LED is a semiconductor device that emits light when an electric current passes through it.
questions.en: What does the abbreviation LED, for a semiconductor device that emits light when current passes through it, stand for?
questions.de: Wofür steht die Abkürzung LED, ein Halbleiterbauelement, das Licht aussendet, wenn Strom hindurchfließt?

timeline.labelEn: Nick Holonyak demonstrates the first visible-light (red) semiconductor diode at General Electric
timeline.labelDe: Nick Holonyak führt bei General Electric die erste Halbleiterdiode mit sichtbarem (rotem) Licht vor

questions.notes: Timeline date from the Nick Holonyak article (GaAsP diode of 9 October 1962, which worked as a red LED at room temperature).

questions.cardText:
[Law] What significant principle was established by the Magna Carta?
A. The king is subject to the law
B. The protection of individual liberties against government infringement
C. Checks and balances
Answer: A. The Magna Carta, signed in 1215, is considered one of the first steps towards constitutional law, influencing many future legal documents, including the United States Constitution and the Bill of Rights.
questions.en: Which significant principle about the king's relationship to the law is the Magna Carta of 1215 credited with establishing?
questions.de: Welcher bedeutende Grundsatz über das Verhältnis des Königs zum Gesetz wird der Magna Carta von 1215 zugeschrieben?
questions.answerEn: That the king is subject to the law
questions.answerDe: Dass auch der König dem Gesetz unterworfen ist

timeline.labelEn: King John of England seals Magna Carta at Runnymede
timeline.labelDe: König Johann von England besiegelt die Magna Carta in Runnymede

questions.notes: Magna Carta was sealed (not signed) by King John on 15 June 1215. Historians note the 1215 charter mainly concerned king and barons; the 'king under the law' principle is how later writers read it (Wikipedia: it 'made the King subject to the common law of the land').
